rulings.dispute: Which community sets the Biome baseline. zoom-out/readiness/catalyst: `biome init` defaults (readiness adds `useIgnoreFile` + scoped `files.includes`); critic/codebase/comprehension: Pi's own block (indentWidth 3, lineWidth 120, Pi's six rule overrides); structural: init with lineWidth 120 as the one traced deviation; structural also calls the spec requirement unmeasurable until a baseline is named. Several lenses mark it for Joel.
rulings.answer: Joel's ruling narrows this but does not settle it. The evidence eliminates everything except one knob. Eliminated: (1) GitHub-majority spaces — re-indents every line of all 20 `src/` files for a knob whose init default is already tab; (2) Pi's `indentWidth: 3` and its six rule overrides — zero measured effect on this tree (identical format output to indentWidth 2; zero lint diagnostics with or without the overrides), so they are dead config and go by the deletion test; (3) init *verbatim* (no `files.includes`, VCS off) — unworkable, see ruling 2. What remains for Joel is a single choice: `lineWidth` 80 (init default) or 120 (Pi and all four Biome-using pi-package extensions). Measured cost on HEAD: 80 → 11 `src/` files reformatted, including three handler files (session-start/tree/compact) whose signature lines wrap; 120 → 4 `src/` files reformatted (pi-archive-adapter, pi-jev-scorer-adapter, tool-call, commit-archived-batch), each a multi-line parameter list collapsed to one line. No width leaves the tree untouched (90→9, 100→1, 110→4). I would choose 120: the adoption audience Joel named is Pi extension authors, where 120 is uniform; it is the smaller reformat; and it is the only deviation from `biome init`, so the spec's 'every non-default setting traces to a named source' scenario has exactly one entry. Everything else in `biome.json` is settled regardless of his answer: `biome init` 2.6.7 output as the base, `vcs.enabled/clientKind: git/useIgnoreFile: true`, `files.includes` scoped (ruling 2), recommended preset, no rule overrides, tab, double quotes, `organizeImports` on. Note for Joel: owner-rulings.md glosses his words as 'not a bespoke or sibling-copied config'; that phrase is the conductor's paraphrase, not his, and readiness leaned on it to exclude Pi's block. The exclusion stands on the deletion test above, not on that gloss.
rulings.evidence: Installed @biomejs/biome 2.6.7, typescript 5.9.3, vitest 5.1.0, @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent 1.5.2 in a `git archive HEAD` copy under mktemp -d (removed after). Ran `biome check . --reporter=summary` with four configs: init verbatim; init + vcs + includes; Pi block + includes; init + lineWidth 120 + vcs + includes. Format-diff file lists: lineWidth 80 → 11 src files; 120 → 4 src files; Pi block and init+120 produced the identical list. Lint diagnostics on src: zero under every config (the only lint hits were `test-jev-poc.mjs` and a planted `.pi/` file). Swept lineWidth 90/100/110 → 9/1/4 files. Viewed the 120-width diffs: all four are param-list or import-list collapses, none semantic. Pi repo package.json via `gh api`: Biome 2.3.5, typescript 7.0.2.

rulings.dispute: Biome file scope: how lint excludes the preserved PoC files and `.pi/` without editing them. critic CR-1 (blocking), structural F3, codebase CC-2, readiness R-03, zoom-out ZO-1, catalyst CAT-1 all want an explicit scope; they disagree on mechanism (`files.includes` allowlist vs `!!` force-ignore vs `vcs.useIgnoreFile`) and leave unverified whether Biome reads `.git/info/exclude` or ignores the lockfile.
rulings.answer: `biome.json` SHALL set `files.includes` to an allowlist: `src/**`, `tests/**`, the root config files (`package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, `biome.json`, `vitest.config.ts`). Negative globs on the PoC filenames are not needed and not wanted. `vcs.useIgnoreFile: true` is set (it is Biome's documented guidance and ~half of configs) but is not the mechanism: it does honour `.git/info/exclude` (measured, contrary to the lenses' unverified assumption), yet that file is local-only and a fresh clone has no `.pi/` exclusion, so the allowlist must carry the scope. `package-lock.json` needs no entry: Biome ignores it by default (measured). `lint` is `biome check .` (read-only); any `format`/`lint:fix` script is a separate script; `check` never passes `--write`. Add the development-checks requirement and a scenario: `npm run lint` reports nothing under `jev-context-poc.ts`, `test-jev-poc.mjs`, `docs/`, `openspec/` or `.pi/`. This closes critic CR-1.
rulings.decided_by: Measurement: Biome 2.6.7 with init config and no `files.includes` checked 45 files including every `.md` under `docs/adr/` and `openspec/changes/` (Biome 2.6 formats Markdown; `research-chidi.md` and all seven council reports were flagged for formatting), both PoC files (format errors in both, plus an `organizeImports` error and a `noUnusedVariables` warning in `test-jev-poc.mjs`), and a planted `.pi/marbleization/junk.js`. With `files.includes` scoped: 22–25 files, zero hits outside `src/`, `tests/` and root json.
rulings.evidence: `npx biome check . --reporter=summary` under init config: 45 files, 29 errors incl. docs/adr/*.md, openspec/changes/foundation-and-packaging/*.md, jev-context-poc.ts, test-jev-poc.mjs, .pi/marbleization/junk.js. Same with `vcs.enabled+useIgnoreFile: true` and `.pi/` only in `.git/info/exclude`: 44 files, `.pi/` absent; `biome check .pi/marbleization/junk.js` → 'paths were provided but ignored'. `biome format package-lock.json` → 'provided but ignored' under every config. With includes `["src/**","tests/**","*.json"]`: 23 files checked, no PoC/.md/.pi entries.

rulings.dispute: Formatting blast radius vs the spec scenario 'only the stub bodies differ' and the proposal's 'Files edited: seven handler files, one stub body each'. critic CR-2, structural F2, readiness R-04, catalyst CAT-2 say a one-time format pass is unavoidable and the scenario must loosen; readiness R-04 and critic CR-8 add that `pi.on(...)` forces a `_pi`→`pi` parameter rename; catalyst adds `_`-prefix normalisation for unused params.
rulings.answer: A one-time `biome check --write` pass over `src/` is in scope under any baseline, because no `lineWidth` leaves HEAD untouched (measured). The extension-packaging scenario 'Signatures unchanged' is reworded to what it means to protect: exported function names, parameter order and types, return types, and the import boundary are unchanged against HEAD; formatter whitespace is permitted. The proposal's Files-edited list widens to the formatted files (4 at lineWidth 120, 11 at 80; exact list per ruling 1's measurement) and the design orders the tasks: format pass first (diff reviewed as whitespace-only), then the no-op edits. The `_pi`→`pi` rename does not happen: `_pi.on("<event>", () => {})` type-checks and passes Biome recommended with zero diagnostics, so Q1(a)'s `pi.on(...)` is shorthand for 'call `.on` on the handler's Pi parameter', and the parameter keeps its HEAD name. No `_`-prefix normalisation is needed: recommended produced zero lint diagnostics on the stubs before or after the edit. No rule overrides are added.
rulings.decided_by: Measurement (ruling 1's lineWidth sweep: 80/90/100/110/120 → 11/9/1/4/4 files; the 120 diffs collapse multi-line param lists in pi-archive-adapter, pi-jev-scorer-adapter, tool-call, commit-archived-batch); `tsc --noEmit` exit 0 and `biome check src tests` clean after replacing all seven throws with `_pi.on(...)`.
rulings.evidence: Applied `sed` in the temp copy replacing each handler's `throw` with `_pi.on("<event>", () => {})`; `tsc --noEmit` → 0 errors (including `context`, whose handler result type accepts a void arrow); `biome check src tests` after `--write` → 'Checked 22 files, No fixes applied', zero lint rules reported. `tool-call.ts` is one of the four files Biome reflows at 120, so 'only stub bodies differ' is false for a handler file even at the widest candidate.

rulings.dispute: Lockfile / package-manager policy vs the scenario 'Install does not dirty the tree'. critic CR-3, readiness R-02, zoom-out ZO-2, comprehension C4: `npm install` creates `package-lock.json`, the proposed `.gitignore` does not cover it, no artifact says whether to commit it; siblings disagree (pi-omlx ignores it, pi-jefferson commits pnpm-lock.yaml).
rulings.answer: npm is the package manager (every script and scenario already says `npm run`; Pi's own repo uses npm). `package-lock.json` is committed in this change and listed as a created file. It is not added to `.gitignore`. The scenario is reworded: on a clean checkout containing the committed lockfile, `npm install` followed by `git status` reports no changes. Biome needs no exclusion for it (ignored by default, ruling 2). pi-omlx's ignore is the outlier against npm's documented default and Pi's practice; the community principle in owner-rulings decides for committing.
rulings.decided_by: Joel's standing principle (owner-rulings 'Biome configuration' entry: decisions reflect the community's preferences) applied to measured community practice: `earendil-works/pi` root has `package-lock.json` committed (`gh api repos/earendil-works/pi/contents`); npm creates the lockfile on install (measured).
rulings.evidence: `npm install` in the temp copy produced `package-lock.json` (resolved typescript 5.9.3, vitest 5.1.0, vite 8.3.8, @types/node 22.20.5, @biomejs/biome 2.6.7, pi-coding-agent 1.5.2). `gh api repos/earendil-works/pi/contents --jq '.[].name'` lists `package-lock.json` and `.npmrc`. `~/Projects/pi-omlx/.gitignore` contains `package-lock.json`; `~/Projects/pi-jefferson` has `pnpm-lock.yaml` and `"packageManager": "pnpm@12.17.0"`.

rulings.dispute: First-test target. codebase CC-1, critic CR-6, structural F4, readiness R-05, zoom-out: my S6 named four 'existing pure functions' but `buildStub` and `formatRecalledContext` still throw; only `shouldArchive` and `selectRecalledIds` are implemented. readiness R-05 further says the change has no test that can go red-then-green and wants an entry test (see ruling 6).
rulings.answer: My S6 was wrong on two of four; corrected. The first domain test targets `shouldArchive(rawTextLength: number, minCharsToArchive: number)` (`src/domain/archived-output.ts:19`) and/or `selectRecalledIds` (`src/domain/recall.ts:13`): equal-to-threshold → included, one below → excluded. The development-checks requirement says 'an implemented pure function'. The `.js` specifier chain is exercised by the import itself (`../../src/domain/archived-output.js`). The test is shown to catch a mistake by the `>=`→`>` mutation.
rulings.decided_by: Source at HEAD: `buildStub` (archived-output.ts:24–26) and `formatRecalledContext` (recall.ts:18–20) are `throw new Error("Not implemented: …")`; `shouldArchive` and `selectRecalledIds` have bodies.
rulings.evidence: Read the four functions at HEAD. In the temp copy, `tests/domain/archived-output.test.ts` asserting `shouldArchive(10,10) === true` and `shouldArchive(9,10) === false` passed under vitest 5.1.0; mutating `>=` to `>` in `archived-output.ts` made it fail; restored → green.

rulings.dispute: Automatable pass/fail signal for 'Load check passes' and 'Seven events registered'. critic CR-4 and readiness R-05 propose a vitest test calling the default export with a recording fake `ExtensionAPI`; comprehension C1 and codebase CC-3 want the packages-route check to prove the package was discovered, not merely that no error printed; readiness R-07 proposes literal commands including `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=<tmp> pi -ne --help`; critic notes `tsc` accepts any valid event name and the `--help` exit code is unmeasured.
rulings.answer: Three parts. (1) The in-repo guard is a vitest test `tests/app/extension/taiknr.test.ts` that invokes the default export with a Proxy fake whose only member is `on` (any other member access throws), and asserts the sorted list of registered events equals exactly the seven names. It runs inside `npm run check`, needs no Pi runtime (every Pi import in `src/` is `import type`), goes red against HEAD's throwing stubs and green after the no-op edit, and catches a valid-but-wrong name (`session_before_tree`) that `tsc` accepts. This is a test, not production mechanism; the design names it. (2) `pi --help` exits 0 whether or not an extension failed to load (measured; `main.js` prints diagnostics then `process.exit(0)` on `parsed.help`), so the manual load check asserts on stderr text — absence of `Failed to load extension` — never on exit code. A non-interactive run would exit 1 on load failure but costs a model call, so it is not used. (3) The packages-route check MUST NOT pass `-ne`: `-ne` disables configured packages, and with it the throwing stub produced no error at all (measured), so readiness R-07's literal command is vacuous. The literal procedure: `D=$(mktemp -d); printf '{"packages":["<abs repo path>"]}' > $D/settings.json; PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=$D pi --no-session --help 2>&1 | rg 'Failed to load extension|Host-provided extension packages'` must print nothing; then `rm -rf $D`. Discovery is proven by a negative control the tasks run once: with one handler's `throw` temporarily restored, the same command prints the `Failed to load extension … Not implemented` line; with the peer temporarily moved to `dependencies`, it prints the `Host-provided extension packages` warning. Both restored before the tick. Record `pi --version` (1.5.2) in the task.
rulings.decided_by: Measurement of Pi 1.5.2: `--help` exit codes, `-ne` behaviour on the packages route, and the recording-fake test's three negative controls. Pi source: `dist/main.js` lines 766–812 (`parsed.help` → `reportDiagnostics` → `process.exit(0)`; `hasRuntimeErrors` → exit 1 only on the non-help path).
rulings.evidence: With throwing stubs: `pi -ne -e <file> --help` exit 0; `pi -ne -e <dir> --help` exit 0; `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=$A pi --no-session --help` exit 0 with stderr 'Failed to load extension … Not implemented: registerSessionStartHandler'; `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=$A pi -ne --no-session --help` exit 0 with empty stderr (package not loaded); `PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR=$A pi --no-session --mode json x` exit 1. `rg 'on\(event: string'` in types.d.ts → no catch-all overload; `_pi.on("sesion_tree")` → TS2769; `_pi.on("session_before_tree")` → tsc 0 errors (real event at types.d.ts:1240). Recording-fake test: green on no-op stubs; red when session-tree's throw was restored ('Not implemented: registerSessionTreeHandler'); red on `session_before_tree` (diff showed the extra name).

rulings.dispute: Version pinning for Biome, vitest and TypeScript. critic CR-5, structural F6, readiness R-06: majors unmeasured; registry latest is typescript 7.0.2 and vitest 5.1.0 while my orientation measured typescript 5.9.3 and `node --test`; Biome docs say install with `-E`.
rulings.answer: Pin what is now measured, and prefer the community's current choice where both pass: `@biomejs/biome` exact `2.6.7` (Biome's documented `npm i -D -E`, `$schema` 2.6.7); `vitest` `^5.1.0` (registry latest; measured green including `.js`→`.ts` resolution and the Proxy-fake test); `typescript` `^7.0.2` (registry latest and Pi's own devDependency; `tsc --noEmit` exit 0 on this tree — 5.9.3 also passes, so either major is safe and the lockfile fixes the exact version); `@types/node` `^22` (Pi pins 22.x; Node engines in Pi `>=22.19.0`). No `engines` field: nothing breaks without it. The design writes `package.json` verbatim and the committed lockfile (ruling 4) makes the run reproducible. Tests import `describe/test/expect` from `vitest`; no `globals` (measured: `tsc` with `tests/**` included and `types: ["node"]` passes that way, and `globals: true` would break it as critic CR-9 said).
rulings.decided_by: Measurement in the temp copy plus Pi's devDependencies (`gh api` on earendil-works/pi package.json: typescript 7.0.2, @types/node 22.19.19) and Biome's install docs (Chidi addendum §1).
rulings.evidence: `npx -y -p typescript@7.0.2 tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` → exit 0, no output; typescript 5.9.3 → exit 0. `npx vitest run` (5.1.0, vite 8.3.8, Node 26.8.1): 2 files passed, including imports through `../../src/app/extension/taiknr.js` and `../../src/domain/archived-output.js`. Full chain `biome check . && tsc --noEmit && vitest run` → exit 0.

rulings.dispute: Settings-entry order and revert in the Migration Plan (readiness R-08), given Q2(a): after Joel adds `../../Projects/pi-taiknr` to `packages`, every Pi session on his machine loads the extension; a checkout of a pre-change commit would make every session print a load error; a revert of the change un-ignores `node_modules/`.
rulings.answer: Design.md's Migration Plan records: (1) merge the change; (2) Joel adds the `packages` entry himself (Q2(a)), after which the extension loads in every Pi session in every project; (3) rollback order is remove the settings entry first, then revert; (4) while the entry is active, checking out a commit before this change turns every Pi session start into a `Failed to load extension … Not implemented` diagnostic (interactive sessions continue; `--print`/`--mode json` runs exit 1), so Joel should not switch the checkout below this change with the entry active; (5) `node_modules/` and `package-lock.json` are left for manual deletion after a revert. No code and no task; this is design text. The settings edit itself stays Joel's and is not a ticked task.
rulings.decided_by: Joel's Q2(a) ruling (owner-rulings.md) for who acts; measurement for the hazard.
rulings.evidence: Throwing-stub load via the packages route: stderr 'Failed to load extension …' on `--help` (exit 0) and exit 1 on `--mode json` (main.js `hasRuntimeErrors` path). Relative path base for `packages` entries is `~/.pi/agent` (Pi `docs/settings.md` line 151), so the entry form `../../Projects/pi-taiknr` matches the two existing sibling entries in Joel's settings.json.

rulings.dispute: Does `biome check` exit non-zero on a warn-severity rule (critic CR-7)? The spec scenario 'a file violates a Biome rule → `npm run check` exits non-zero' is only true for error severity unless `--error-on-warnings` is added (rpiv-mono's pattern).
rulings.answer: Narrow the scenario to 'violates an error-severity Biome rule or formatting'. Do not add `--error-on-warnings`: default Biome exit behaviour is the community behaviour (one extension of five uses the flag), and nothing in this change needs it.
rulings.decided_by: Measurement of Biome 2.6.7 exit codes; Joel's community principle (owner-rulings).
rulings.evidence: A test file with an unused `const` (recommended `noUnusedVariables`, warn): `biome check` exit 0; `biome check --error-on-warnings` exit 1.

rulings.dispute: Test discovery scope (structural F5, comprehension C5, catalyst CAT-1): the spec says the test command 'runs only files under `tests/`', but config-free vitest's default include matches any `*.test.ts` anywhere; the proposal hedges 'a vitest configuration if the design needs one'; catalyst proposes `vitest run tests` with no config file.
rulings.answer: Add `vitest.config.ts` with `test.include: ["tests/**/*.test.ts"]` and nothing else, and drop the proposal's hedge. This makes the spec's invariant true as written, mirrors `tsconfig.json`'s `include`, and is what pi-omlx, rpiv-mono and pi-mcp-adapter do. `vitest.config.ts` is added to Biome's `files.includes` by name (not via `*.ts`, which would admit `jev-context-poc.ts`). The PoC files are already outside the default include (no `.test.`/`.spec.` segment, Chidi addendum §4), so the explicit include is for the stated invariant, not for PoC safety. Comprehension C3: the spec scenario 'Node resolves the chain' is reworded to 'the test runner resolves the chain'; plain-Node resolution is measured (Node 26.8.1 `import()` of a `.ts` through a `.js` specifier works) but is not a requirement of this change.
rulings.decided_by: Joel's community principle (3 of 5 configured pi-package extensions set an explicit include, Chidi addendum §4); measurement that the default include and the explicit include both find `tests/**/*.test.ts` and neither runs the PoC files.
rulings.evidence: `npx vitest run` with no config found `tests/app/taiknr.test.ts` and `tests/domain/archived-output.test.ts` (2 passed) and did not run `test-jev-poc.mjs` (no model call, 83 ms total). Node resolution measured in the orientation pass: `node -e 'import("./src/use-cases/stage-tool-outputs.ts")'` resolved `../domain/archived-output.js`.

rulings.dispute: Unobservable spec scenario (readiness R-09): 'Pi loads only the entry named in `pi.extensions` and does not scan the conventional resource directories' asserts a Pi internal no repository check can observe.
rulings.answer: Reword the scenario to what the repository controls and a test can assert: `package.json` `pi.extensions` equals `["./src/app/extension/taiknr.ts"]`, and no root `index.ts` or `extensions/` directory exists. Cite Chidi §4 (`collectPackageResources`: when the manifest has any resource field, only those entries are used) for the Pi-side behaviour instead of asserting it as a scenario. My orientation Trap 7 already measured that a planted `tests/foo.test.ts` never executed under either load route.
rulings.evidence: Re-read Chidi §4 against `package-manager.js` lines ~2000–2030 (`collectPackageResources` → `addManifestEntries` when manifest entries exist). Orientation Trap 7 measurement stands; not repeated.
